answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a bonded work-graph rather than cheap sign-ups. Each identity locks a deposit that is slashed if a cluster of correlated accounts is proven. New agents must wander across unrelated tasks over many epochs, so a factory of clones cannot appear all at once. When votes or attestations echo in lockstep, peers inspect the public knoll of recent trails—timing, stake, and counterparties—and refuse to countersign the duplicates. One bond, one slowly earned trail, one vote.
